contract: Words, individual forms, grammar teaching/reference and English scenarios are prescribed. New assessments use practical Pashto only; shortages use vocabulary or approved phrases, never English rule quizzes. Every instructional Pashto clause is compiled; no sentence targets or authored fallbacks.

days.title: It / Things
days.intro: Complete School with Ms Hameed first. Then study Home, Nature and Market in any order, or explicitly skip to the daily challenge.
days.challenge: Muhammad Jan welcomes you and prepares your home handover.
grammar: A description places a noun before an adjective and a present equative. Choose the equative and adjective form that agree with the noun. Feminine singular, masculine singular and inherent plural nouns have different agreement.

days.title: He / She
days.intro: Complete School with Ms Hameed first. Then study Home, Nature and Market in any order, or explicitly skip to the daily challenge.
days.challenge: Use he and she with present action and possession clauses in Subject–Object–Verb order.
grammar: A present action clause normally puts the subject first, the object next and the complete finite verb last. Third-person singular verbs describe he, she or one named person. Learn each evidenced conjugation as a complete form.

days.title: This One or That One?
days.intro: Complete School with Ms Hameed first. Then study Home, Nature and Market in any order, or explicitly skip to the daily challenge.
days.challenge: Deena describes nearby and distant objects at the lakeside; player identifies intended objects and constructs demonstrative sentences.
grammar: Near and far demonstratives can point to an object or stand independently. Keep their deictic function separate from the personal pronoun with the same spelling. Adjectives inside a noun phrase precede the noun.

days.title: Where Is Medina’s Notebook?
days.intro: Complete School with Ms Hameed first. Then study Home, Nature and Market in any order, or explicitly skip to the daily challenge.
days.challenge: Medina retraces her route. Questions describe locations; the player interprets clues to identify the notebook’s location through dialogue only.
